Let g(x) = x²f(x) − 1. It has degree 9 and vanishes at h(i) = i(i+1) for i = 1,…,8, so g(x) = (cx + d)·P(x), where P(x) = ∏(x − h(i)).

Since x² divides x²f(x), we need g(0) = −1 and g′(0) = 0.

- Let H = ∏h(i). P(0) = H, because there are 8 factors and the signs cancel. So g(0) = dH = −1, giving d = −1/H.
- P′(0)/P(0) = −Σ1/h(i) = −Σ1/(i(i+1)) = −(1 − 1/9) = −8/9.
- g′(0) = cH + dP′(0) = 0 gives c = (8/9)d.

Therefore g(x) = −(1/H)(1 + 8x/9)P(x).

At x = 90, the factor 1 + 8·90/9 equals 81. Then

g(90) = −81·∏(90 − h(i))/h(i).

Since 90 − i(i+1) = (9−i)(10+i), the product is

∏(9−i)(10+i) / ∏ i(i+1) = (8!·18!/10!)/(8!·9!) = 18!/(10!·9!) = 48620/10 = 4862.

So g(90) = −81·4862, and

f(90) − 1/90² = g(90)/90² = −81·4862/8100 = −4862/100 = −2431/50.
